## Purpose and status

Build on PR173's forced dyadic band and connect it to the repository's coefficient, complete-certificate, and invariant-component programs. **Full Collatz remains OPEN.**

The broader reassessment inventories all 145 PRs returned through PR186 and adds three Lean modules with **38 audited public statements**, following the earlier four-module, 53-statement continuation. The combined **91 statements across seven added modules** are an audit inventory, not a count of 91 novel mathematical theorems. Written analytic results are separated from kernel-checked results.

**Published head:** `2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737`  
**Tree:** `4e8f9b030e02ece2d6697857c691ef1815725393`

The PR remains stacked on PR173. The baseline forced-section sources are frozen at `fa0c9e2a2851e6324391e39c17afcb5913185aec`. Subsequent research is in progress; no unpublished argument is included in the claims below.

## New kernel-checked finite coefficient theorem

For the ordinary shortcut map, let q_t(n) count odd inputs in the first t steps and C_t(n)=3^q_t(n)/2^t. For every B>=1, define

```
k = 70*(floor(log_2 B)+3)
M = 2^k
N = n+M+1
H = 6*B^2*(n+N)+1.
```

The proof gives the unconditional, finite alternative

```
exists t<=H: C_t(n)<1 or C_t(n)>B.
```

It also checks H<=12*B^2*n+6*2^210*B^72+6*B^2+1. The constants are deliberately conservative.

The proof uses the exact full-residue moment sum 2^q_k(r)=3^k, an integer residue-packing bound, and the complete affine correction. Required finite injectivity is derived inside the argument by ruling out a repetition under the provisional strip hypothesis; nonperiodicity is not assumed.

PR92 already supplied a stronger qualitative escape statement on nonperiodic ordinary orbits. The contribution here is the elementary **finite integer Lean proof with an explicit uniform horizon**. Upper exits remain possible, and a lower coefficient crossing still needs its affine displacement condition.

[CoefficientCounting.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/CoefficientCounting.lean) · [CoefficientPeaks.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/CoefficientPeaks.lean) · [Proof and prior overlap](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/COEFFICIENT_PEAKS.md)

## New complete-certificate boundary rule

Given a complete odd-gap certificate for 4p+1 beginning with gap four and arbitrary suffix tail, and the explicit guards

```
3 does not divide p; p!=1; p mod9!=7; p mod27!=19,
```

the proof constructs a complete certificate for an odd predecessor z>=2p+1 with a prefix W of gaps at most three, followed by 2::tail. The whole suffix is retained literally.

For S=4(4p+1) and S'=8z, the checked result gives S'>=S+4 while the highest-changed-multiplicity grade strictly decreases:

```
[5,8] + grades(tail)
    -> [7] + grades(W) + [4] + grades(tail).
```

Every inserted grade is at most seven; one grade eight disappears. Every target 0<t<=2S+1 remains unchanged inside the child interval. The interval theorem retains its explicit lower-rank induction hypothesis. This is a successful guarded rule, not a complete dispatcher.

The local certificate semantics and rank definitions are checked independently; the exact mathematical crosswalk to PR177 is written and source-qualified, not a direct import of PR177's full Lean graph.

The companion audit distinguishes the unconditional family T^8(768r+295)=729r+281<768r+295 from remaining guard failures. Its bounded replay of 1055 first descending at clock80 is explicitly not counted as a Lean theorem or a counterexample to convergence.

[CertificateBoundary.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/CertificateBoundary.lean) · [Proof and interface](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/CERTIFICATE_BOUNDARY.md) · [Guard-composition audit](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/GUARD_COMPOSITION_AUDIT.md)

## New reviewed written rigidity theorem

For a nonconstant Boolean ordinary invariant label f(Tn)=f(n), there is one epsilon_f>0 such that every [0,1]-valued periodic p of period 2^a*3^b satisfies

```
liminf_X (1/H_X) sum_{n<=X} |f(n)-p(n)|/n >= epsilon_f.
```

The same positive constant is independent of the conductor and of p. Thus qualitative approximation in logarithmic mean already forces constancy; the earlier fast approximation rate is unnecessary. The natural-mean consequence uses a limsup, not a liminf.

This is a **source-qualified written measure-theoretic theorem, not Lean verification**. It uses Tao's marginal fine-scale mixing and the older selected atom FLOOR and logarithmic predecessor result LOG. It does not need the newer joint-clock positive-natural-density claim.

The proof uses finite periodic stationary densities on actual original integers, a total-variation coherent limit, exact ordinary branch changes, and mixing of the compact skew system. It never evaluates an arbitrary almost-everywhere limiting density at an ordinary integer.

An independent adversarial review passed the exact final proof and separately reconstructed FLOOR/LOG. The missing step is construction of the required approximants for the basin-of-one label. Compact cylinder density does not provide that construction.

[PROFINITE_LABEL_RIGIDITY.md](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/PROFINITE_LABEL_RIGIDITY.md)

## Separate audit of the stronger predecessor-population claim

The [audit](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/PREDECESSOR_POPULATION_AUDIT.md) freezes PR180 at `d0349de2108abb7c8fb8393c086610e3372df116` and its selected-prefix parent at `f87cb69b3dd86257731ddfbab58c87bf3b5f63d6`. It found no unsupported step in the specified written chain giving a uniform lower count cX/a for actual odd predecessors of a ternary-unit target when X>=Ca.

The chain checks Tao's nonnegative Fourier envelope, joint clock slicing, the fixed-total residue-counting operator, uniform clock convolution, and removal of cross-depth duplicates through a nonperiodic parent. This is a major source-qualified written result, not a new Lean proof or blanket acceptance of PR180. The second analytic reviewer checked the marginal FLOOR/LOG chain needed for rigidity; that review is not represented as a second full audit of the joint-clock population argument.

## Retained earlier continuation

The earlier 53-statement checkpoint remains unchanged:

- Power-saving marked returns y^120<n^119 on arbitrarily large simultaneous exponent blocks for short certified odd offsets; the r=1 specialization has upper exponent density at least5/6 along arbitrarily large cutoffs.
- The finite temporal bound (floor(log_2 N)+1)*V_n(N)<=196608*N for N distinct observed odd states, with no assumed escape rate.
- Exact necessary initial valuation cover v_2(9n+1) in {2,3,5,7} for an original source with no strict descent.
- A kernel-checked first-band entry from n=2^601-1 whose canonical offset exceeds n.

Their source-dependent scope and actual earlier execution evidence are preserved in the [previous published PR description](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/reassessment/PR182_BEFORE.json) and [continuation report](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2d478a6588f33a72fc3a5bdc085a928b5cf78737/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/README.md).

## Validation actually executed

- Lean4.34.1, compiler commit `5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52`; tracked-clean Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`.
- Fresh reassessment replay: both pinned prerequisite modules, all three new proof modules, and the complete 38-statement audit; six successful commands, sequential -j1, warningAsError=true. No prebuilt local proof module was reused in this replay.
- All38 new public statements depend only on subsets of propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry, native_decide, or custom convergence axiom supplies these results.
- Earlier53 audit statements and their original receipts remain unchanged. Source hashes for both packets were bound again to publication.
- Separate internal agents independently reviewed the finite coefficient proof, certificate rewrite, and written rigidity proof. Review scope and exact byte hashes are retained.
- The five required repository checks passed on the clean local proof checkout and again on this **actual published head**, with **381 tracked files** and unchanged checkout identity. These checks verify repository integrity, separately from the Lean kernel.

## Exact remaining closing obligations

A full proof still needs a universal successful source/certificate reduction, exclusion of the all-supercritical coefficient alternative with full affine corrections, a retained-source transport estimate that forces absorption, or a proved regularity property of the actual basin label. The new theorem families and density statements do not establish any of those universal conclusions.
